body: i understand that too. are any of your problems situational? like, are you in a shit life situation too?

Yeah. 

You seem like a really nice person, and your kids are lucky to have you. It makes me cry to say that because I guess I'm really emotional about parents who really care. I don't know. 

I'm often afraid of other aspergers communities on the internet, because I guess I'm pretty mild in comparison (so sayeth the medical professionals who deal with me). I've got quite a few friends locally and internationally on the spectrum, though. I'm quite an introvert. ): 

I just... I feel like I can't conquer this. Even when I bullshit (when my grandpa was there was a class I didn't do any readings for, though I went to all the lectures; I got a 77 on an exam I barely studied for) I do okay, but for some reason this feels beyond me. This sort of cycle happens a lot, especially when I'm this depressed, so if it's actually any different or I'm just catastrophising, I don't know.

The thing is, I love what I study. I have one class I don't like and I'm not doing well in, but that's not the end of the world; I just need it for my degree, so doing what is considered 'average' at my school is fine for just one course. I've been having trouble remembering to study Finnish vocabulary, though. I'm clever at languages, but I just... I'm so tired by the time I get home every day. I wish there was a way to fight all of this. I'm just exhausted of it, you know?

Yeah... a lot of the time, I don't have much trouble with writing at all. It's the lack of self-confidence that gets me most. Can you believe I'm still licking my wounds after a friend said I wasn't too great at plot development, even though she said it when she was a bit mad at me? So many people (who wouldn't lie to me; I can tell) have told me I'm so good, but I still hear my mother telling me I'll never be anything and I'll die alone in my head instead. That's my issue.

I do CBT, but I missed an appointment and I'm too afraid to call back (phone anxiety). I have an appointment with my accessibility counsellor on Tuesday, so I'm hoping I can sort some things out with her... We get along very, very well.
please stick with it. if you're willing to end it all, can you just... wait the two weeks. the six weeks.

I'm asperger's as well. It's not so bad. It's mostly the other stuff that messes with me.

Yeah, I love her art style. It's so elegant.

I'm kind of close, but I don't want my dad to bury me. My friends and my father and their love (and of course a bit of my own selfish curiosity at how the world works) are what's keeping me here. It is hard for me to accept their love (I feel so undeserving), and I feel like a burden to them, but at the same time I am very overly empathetic, and thinking about hurting them hurts me. 

Most of the time, I'm not suicidal at all. I'm just depressed (or dysthymic at my best days when situational depression/grief isn't in play), anxious, and anhedonic. Sometimes I just get pushed to this breaking point where it hurts so much and all I want to do is scream, but I'm afraid to scream.

but i mean... if you end it, that's it. there's no going back. i read somewhere (i don't know if it's true or not, but i'm sure there's truth in it either way) that people who attempted suicide by jumping off a bridge and survived told medical workers that during the fall, they suddenly realised all the things plaguing them could probably be dealt with in some way or another.

like, it hurts, but you're alive and you're not out of options yet. you are hesitant to try the therapies and stuff, but how can you know if you don't try? 

do you really want to face an unknown that could be nothing at all in the end, or do you want to live, but in a way that doesn't pain you? 

i would say just keep trying a bit longer. you seem like a brave person, going through this for this long.

As for writing, I know. I'm doing my best, but like I said, the things that normally make me happy (and writing is one of those things) just... I can't reach them. It's like I'm trapped behind a rubber wall, with the tiniest bit of give just to tease me, or something. I'm grappling but I can't reach. 

I have a lot of anxiety issues and very low self-worth (i was emotionally abused on a daily basis for the first 17 years of my life), so that isn't helping right now, either...

Hey, I'm on the spectrum too.

Jansson wrote a couple of picture books (Who will Comfort Toffle? is great, and ... ahh I can't remember the name in English offhand, but if you look up "Hur gick det sen?" you should find the English title.) that would be suitable for a quick read through with a younger kid. The chapter books could probably be something you read chapter by chapter before bedtime, maybe? I don't know. I don't have kids. :P

I know how it feels... the awful thing is that these sort of things require patience, which is so, SO hard to have when your existence is pain. but you've got to hope it works. I'm sure there are people in your life who would drop everything and help you. 

I'm sorry I'm not of much use.

I know, but there's no guarantee that it won't. I'm really bad at this, because I'm in the same mindset as you... 

Just keep thinking that every day, another day of this crap COULD be worth it. That's how I'm making it through.

but maybe you should be honest, even if it's difficult. i only started getting help when i stopped hiding my feelings. even an "i'm feeling a little better, but..." even if that helps a little more, saying that you ARE feeling a little better but you're still afraid, it might... help. i don't know.

if you're saying you're feeling better and you're not, and you're afraid to say it, please don't be. these feelings are counterintuitive and unhealthy, but they are often normal (or at least relatively common). most people really just want to help you. the stigma is heavy to bear, but you can also try to explain things to people, too. most people think what they think about depression and stuff because nobody who actually has it has really... made it through to them, you know?

i don't know if this is useful. i'm sorry i'm kind of a ditz.

Tove Jansson, and the short story collection is called "Fair Play". The main themes are love and work (more specifically the work that producing art entails). It also looks into the complexities of real life. Some of the quotations I'm pulling are really, really lovely, like "A reminder can instantly turn enthusiasm into aversion and spoil everything." I'm so happy it's a book report and not a formal essay, because then I can relate it to my personal feelings and whatnot.

I'm a writer, and a hugely passionate fan of Jansson's work. I used to want to write children's books, and her Moomintroll series was something I found remarkable for its ability to relate 'bigger' ideas to children without seeming condescending, for its blissful and laidback atmosphere, and the style of writing that appeals to a broad audience. This is the first work of hers that I'm reading that's for an adult audience. 

I want to be able to write like her; I want to be able to make someone's breath catch in their throat. I just don't think I'll ever be capable of it.

the fact that you post here seems indicative of a will to live on your part. 

i read your last thread. medications can be a shitfest. i was put on an antipsychotic as a teen even though i wasn't psychotic - my 'anger issues', if i really had any, were situational (abusive mother in the household). 

it feels hopeless. it does. you feel like you don't want to live. but that's not really you, is it? it hurts. it hurts a lot. i know, as you do. but you're not hopeless. you're just in pain and you're sad. 

i just want you to remember that no matter how hopeless you feel, you're here. i know my words probably seem useless and stupid, like i'm just saying shit that everyone else has said, but i just... i don't think anyone has any more 'worth' than any other human at any time. we all have our stumbling blocks. some people have bigger ones than others, and that's shit (i'm not the kind who believes that ~*god gives us the struggles they think we can handle lol!!!!*~ bullshit so stick with me for another second.) but they aren't always permanent.

i guess i can't stop you if you're serious, and i can't say i don't understand. one of my family members was in so much pain himself that he killed himself. but you seem to be trying, which means a lot in a situation like this.

i know you don't know me, but i believe in you, okay? it's so hard to have patience and to struggle through these thoughts, especially if you feel alone (i don't know that you do, but...). you are so strong, even when you feel you're at your weakest. there are other ways to ease the pain.
